correctness.rationale: A fixed point of a simplicial involution has equal barycentric weights on the two vertices of each exchanged orbit; the admissible-orbit complex is a genuine triangulation of the geometric fixed locus. For the torus l1 metric, singleton fixed orbits are diagonal D_i; a two-point (i,j)/(j,i) orbit has diameter 2δ_n(i,j), so at r=2 only adjacent pairs E_i appear. Direct cross-orbit distances yield exactly D_i~D_(i±1), E_i~E_(i±1), D_i~E_i and D_i~E_(i−1). The flag-complex triangles are precisely {D_i,D_(i+1),E_i}, {D_(i+1),E_i,E_(i+1)}; no four-clique exists for n>=7. These form two cyclic boundary rings joined by a triangulated annular strip, giving S1×[0,1], integral H0=H1=Z and no higher homology. At r<2 no pair orbit or diagonal edge survives, giving n discrete points. Scale interval is only [0,2], no claims above r=2.
residual_risks: The result is about geometric fixed points, not only vertexwise fixed diagonals; the orbit-barycenter triangulation is essential.
The all-n reasoning uses n>=7 to prevent short-cycle neighbor coincidences; finite enumeration alone would not justify extrapolation.
